paper.title_en: An adaptive key distribution scheme based on QBER-driven and quantum-chaos synergy
paper.abstract_en: Quantum key distribution (QKD) technology provides a theoretically unconditionally secure key source for information security. However, in practical systems, noise during the transmission of quantum bits-measured by the quantum bit error rate (QBER)-can compromise key security. To address this issue, this paper proposes an encryption scheme that integrates quantum key distribution with chaotic mapping: By extracting multi-dimensional features from QBER time series, the system adaptively selects the optimal chaotic mapping and dynamically adjusts its parameters to generate a high-entropy random key stream sequence. A random forest classifier is used to intelligently select the chaotic mapping, and the effectiveness of the scheme is validated through multi-dimensional randomness measurement and security analysis. Experimental results show that the system maintains high key entropy characteristics across different noise environments, achieves a key generation rate that meets real-time communication requirements, and exhibits better resistance to known-plaintext attacks compared to traditional fixed-parameter chaotic encryption systems.
